slides.headline: OrcaSlicer just dropped its biggest update
body: OrcaSlicer is the free, open-source slicer a lot of Bambu, Snapmaker and Creality owners use instead of the stock one.
On Oct 16 it released the 2.5 alpha: more than 950 pull requests from over 140 contributors.

slides.headline: What’s new
hits: Color mixing: blend 2–3 filaments into new colors
Design tab: basic parametric CAD in the slicer
Python plugins to add your own features
Texture Displacement: real surface texture from images

slides.headline: Good news for Bambu printers
body: Full support for the H2C and A2L, including multicolor printing on the H2C.
On the H2D and X2D you can run different nozzle sizes on the left and right, and pick Standard or High Flow for each nozzle.

slides.headline: Belt printers and IDEX too
body: Belt printers are now supported, so parts can be longer than the machine itself.
Printers with independent dual heads (IDEX) can print two to four copies at the same time.

slides.headline: It’s an alpha. Be careful.
body: Expect bugs, and back up your projects and profiles first.
Want the CAD tab? Go to Preferences → General → Features, tick “CAD feature”, then restart.

slides.headline: How we’ll use it
body: We slice everything in OrcaSlicer and Snapmaker Orca for our Bambu and Snapmaker printers.
slides.take: Color mixing is the one we can’t wait to try. Customer jobs stay on the stable version until 2.5 is out of alpha.
